newsitem.title: JAPAN: POLL - Japan June c/a surplus seen rising 43 pct.
newsitem.headline: POLL - Japan June c/a surplus seen rising 43 pct.

text.p: Japan's current account surplus is expected to show a 43 percent rise in June from a year earlier, although the increase will be smaller than in recent months, according to an average of economists' forecasts.
Forecasts for the increase ranged from 29 percent to 68 percent, or a surplus of 840 billion yen to 1.1 trillion yen.
Economists said a slightly bigger flow of imports should push down the surplus's rate of growth from the hefty rises in May, when it surged 155 percent, and April, which saw a 93 percent rise.

Customs-cleared trade data for June released last month showed imports rising 8.7 percent from a year earlier against an increase in exports of 12.5 percent. The trade surplus itself rose 27.7 percent.
Japan's Ministry of Finance will release the June current account data at 8.50 a.m. Thursday (2350 GMT Wednesday).

Some economists said the rise in imports represented a nascent although not necessarily strong comeback in domestic demand after a sales tax increase to five percent from three percent on April 1 dampened demand for imported goods.
All the economists agreed that the surplus was likely to remain on a rising trend, with many revising their earlier predictions of a significant slowdown in growth in the coming months.

"It's hard to predict the pace of increase but the slowdown that we predicted last month has less of a chance of happening," said Yuriko Tanaka at Goldman Sachs. Like many economists, she pointed to higher car inventories and weak domestic demand that left carmakers little choice but to export.
Richard Jerram, an economist at ING Barings, said that while the surplus had not reached levels that might boost U.S. displeasure into the danger zone, U.S.-Japan tensions were definitely rising.
"As the smoke clears, it's becoming more and more evident that the surplus is on an upward trend," he said.
The following is a breakdown of economists' forecasts for the unadjusted June current account surplus:
Yamaichi Research 840.0 billion yen
NCB Research 851.0 billion yen
Goldman Sachs 864.0 billion yen
IBJ 880.0 billion yen
Daiwa Bank Rsch 897.5 billion yen
ING Barings 905.0 billion yen
BZW Securities 942.0 billion yen
Merrill Lynch 965.0 billion yen
Deutsche Morgan 1.08 trillion yen
Nikko Research 1.10 trillion yen
